package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of struts2-core contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the HttpParameters class. Due to improper case-insensitive handling of HTTP parameter names, attackers can bypass security checks and inject malicious input that is executed on the server. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code, leading to full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: During HTTP request processing at runtime, when user-supplied parameters are parsed and handled by the framework.
required_permissions: filesystem (to read/write files if payload executes file operations)
process_execution (to spawn processes if payload is executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code performs case-insensitive comparison of HTTP parameter names using equalsIgnoreCase, allowing attackers to supply parameters with varying case to bypass security checks. The parameter value is then processed and executed without proper validation or sanitization, enabling arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accepts user-supplied HTTP parameters and, after a case-insensitive match, directly executes the parameter value without any input validation or sanitization. This creates a direct path for attackers to inject and execute malicious payloads by manipulating parameter names and values in HTTP requests.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure web frameworks are expected to strictly validate and sanitize all user input, especially before any code execution. The actual behavior here allows user input to be executed as code based solely on a case-insensitive parameter name match, violating fundamental security principles and enabling RCE.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Case-insensitive parameter handling may be used for user convenience in non-security-critical contexts, such as form field normalization. However, it is never appropriate to use such logic for security-sensitive operations or to determine whether to execute code based on user input.
key_indicators: Use of equalsIgnoreCase for security-relevant parameter checks
Direct execution of user-supplied parameter values
Absence of input validation or sanitization before code execution
Parameter-based control flow leading to code execution

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a specially formed HTTP request with parameter names that exploit case-insensitive handling (e.g., using different casing to bypass security filters).
attack_chain.leads_to: Bypass of security checks and injection of malicious input into the application.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable HttpParameters class processes the malicious parameter, matches it using equalsIgnoreCase, and passes the attacker-controlled value to a code execution path without validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-supplied code on the server (remote code execution).

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote control of the server, enabling actions such as data theft, lateral movement within the network, or further compromise of the environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, data exfiltration, or use of the server as a launch point for additional attacks.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests with parameter names that differ only in case, especially targeting .action endpoints
Unexpected process execution or command invocation by the web server process following HTTP requests
Application logs showing code execution paths triggered by HTTP parameter values
Stack traces referencing org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.HttpParameters during request handling
file_indicators: Presence of struts2-core versions 2.0.0-2.5.2 or 6.0.0-6.3.0.1 in application dependencies
References to org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/HttpParameters.java in stack traces or error logs
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with suspicious or malformed parameters differing only in case
Outbound network connections initiated by the web server process shortly after receiving such requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic for requests with parameter names that differ only in case, particularly those targeting .action endpoints. Scan your software inventory for the presence of vulnerable struts2-core versions. Review application and server logs for evidence of unexpected code execution, process spawning, or stack traces referencing HttpParameters. Deploy web application firewalls (WAFs) with rules to block suspicious parameter patterns, and use runtime application self-protection (RASP) to detect and prevent exploitation attempts in real time.
